analysis:
The change to .github/workflows/release-provider.yml has two parts. It moves five Linux jobs from the Blacksmith runner label (blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404) to GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04: resolve-env (head line 135), qualify-sdk (304), stage-release (1211) and publish-release (1320), plus the corresponding base lines. It also adds timeout-minutes: 90 to build-and-release (head line 343).

Release credentials: stage-release and publish-release hold the R2 keys, the coordinator release key (A-005) and the contents:write token. They now run on GitHub-hosted runners, which are ephemeral and run in isolated VMs. I found no regression from this; the trust model is arguably the same or stronger. The runner label is the only changed line in those jobs.

Unchanged controls in the supplied text:
- Tool installation uses hash-pinned wheels, installed before secrets are resolved.
- Secrets are scoped by environment, and PROD_/legacy values are empty outside prod.
- The artifact download is verified by id, digest and run id.
- Actions are pinned by SHA.
- resolve-env still checks out master and runs verify-source before any credential is used.
- Source gating and the publication concurrency group are unchanged.

The timeout on build-and-release bounds hung signing jobs. That is an availability improvement, and it also limits how long the signing identity and keychain stay exposed. A 90-minute limit could in principle cancel a long notarization. In that case the unconditional cleanup step has if: always(), which still runs after a timeout. This is an availability trade-off, not a security regression.

Related threats are T-034/T-054 (code identity and qualified builds) and the A-011 binary hash registry. The runner change does not alter the signing or registration flow. Unverified: the contents of scripts/provider-release-publication.py and verify-source were not supplied. Also not supplied are any repository runner-group or network-egress policies tied to Blacksmith versus GitHub-hosted runners. Neither affects the conclusion of this diff.
